say: You give it a line segment $[AB]$. It splits it into **equal parts** with no ruler marks, only a compass and straight edge.
The key idea: equal steps along a slanted ray, joined back to $B$ with parallel lines, cut $[AB]$ into equal steps too.

example.question: Divide the segment $[AB]$ into three equal parts using only a compass and straight edge. Show your construction lines.

steps.title: Draw a slanted ray
steps.say: Start at $A$. Draw a ray from $A$ at any angle to $[AB]$. Make it fairly long.

lines.text: With the straight edge, draw a ray from $A$ going up and to the right.

steps.title: Step off three equal arcs
steps.say: Set the compass to any small width. Do not change it again.

lines.text: With the compass point on $A$, draw an arc across the ray. Call the crossing $1$.
Move the point to $1$ and, keeping the same width, draw another arc. Call the crossing $2$.
Move the point to $2$, same width, and mark $3$.

steps.title: Join the last mark to B
steps.say: The three arcs are equal. Join $3$ to $B$.

lines.text: With the straight edge, draw the line from $3$ to $B$.

steps.title: Draw two parallel lines
steps.say: Copy the angle at $3$ to the points $2$ and $1$, so each new line is parallel to $[3B]$.

lines.text: Through $2$, draw a line parallel to $[3B]$. It meets $[AB]$ at $Q$.
Through $1$, draw a line parallel to $[3B]$. It meets $[AB]$ at $P$.
Then $|AP| = |PQ| = |QB|$. Leave all arcs and lines showing.

say: You give it a line segment $[AB]$. It builds an angle of **60°** at $A$ with no protractor and no set square.
The key idea: a triangle with three equal sides has three angles of $60^\circ$, and a compass makes equal sides.

example.question: Using only a compass and straight edge, construct an angle of $60^\circ$ at the point $A$ on the line $[AB]$.

steps.title: Fix the compass width
steps.say: Open the compass to the length $|AB|$. Keep it this width for the whole construction.

lines.text: Place the compass point on $A$ and the pencil on $B$.

steps.title: Draw the first arc
steps.say: The point $C$ must be $|AB|$ from $A$, so it lies on an arc centred at $A$.

lines.text: With the compass point on $A$, draw a long arc above the line.

steps.title: Draw the second arc
steps.say: The point $C$ must also be $|AB|$ from $B$. The two arcs cross at $C$.

lines.text: With the compass point on $B$, same width, draw an arc that crosses the first. Call the crossing $C$.
With the straight edge, draw $[AC]$.
Every angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^\circ$, so $|\angle BAC| = 60^\circ$.
Leave both arcs showing.

say: You give it two side lengths and the angle between them. It builds the **parallelogram** to exact size.
The key idea: opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so the fourth corner is where two arcs, one from each end, cross.
what.in: two sides and the angle between them

how.ordinary: Ordinary level has set it as part (a) of a Paper 2 Question 6 (2023, 15 marks), followed by angle work on the parallelogram's properties.

example.question: Construct the parallelogram $ABCD$ with $|AB| = 6$ cm, $|AD| = 4$ cm and $|\angle DAB| = 70^\circ$.

steps.title: Draw the base
steps.say: Start with the side you are given first. Draw it on the horizontal so the angle is easy to measure.

lines.text: With the ruler, draw $[AB]$ of length $6$ cm.

steps.title: Measure the angle at A
steps.say: The angle sits at $A$, between $[AB]$ and $[AD]$.

lines.text: Put the protractor centre on $A$ with its base along $[AB]$.
Mark $70^\circ$ and draw a ray from $A$ through the mark.

steps.title: Mark D
steps.say: $D$ is on that ray, $4$ cm from $A$.

lines.text: With the ruler, measure $4$ cm along the ray from $A$. Label it $D$.

steps.title: Find C with two arcs
steps.say: Opposite sides are equal, so $|BC| = 4$ cm and $|DC| = 6$ cm.

lines.text: With the compass point on $B$, open to $4$ cm and draw an arc.
With the compass point on $D$, open to $6$ cm and draw an arc that crosses it. Label the crossing $C$.
Draw $[BC]$, $[CD]$. Label every corner and leave the arcs showing.

say: You give it a triangle. It finds the **circumcentre** and draws the circle that passes through all three corners.
The key idea: every point on the perpendicular bisector of a side is the same distance from both ends of that side, so where two bisectors meet is the same distance from all three corners.

how.higher: Higher level has set it as part (a) of a Paper 2 Question 6 (2022, 15 marks), where you find and label the circumcentre.
how.ordinary: Ordinary level has set it as part (a)(ii) of a Paper 2 Question 6 (2021, 10 marks), after a perpendicular bisector of one side.

example.question: Construct the circumcentre and circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 7$ cm, $|BC| = 6$ cm and $|AC| = 5$ cm. Use a compass and straight edge and show your construction lines.

steps.title: Draw the triangle
steps.say: Draw the longest side first, then find the third corner with two arcs.

lines.text: Draw $[AB]$ of length $7$ cm.
From $A$, draw an arc of radius $5$ cm. From $B$, draw an arc of radius $6$ cm. Label the crossing $C$ and join up the triangle.

steps.title: Bisect the first side
steps.say: The circumcentre is the same distance from $A$ and $B$, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of $[AB]$.

lines.text: Open the compass past half of $|AB|$. Draw an arc above and below $[AB]$ from $A$, then from $B$ with the same width.
Join the two crossings with the straight edge.

steps.title: Bisect a second side
steps.say: It is also the same distance from $A$ and $C$, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of $[AC]$.

lines.text: Repeat the construction on $[AC]$.
The two bisectors cross. Label that point $O$.

steps.title: Draw the circle
steps.say: $O$ is the same distance from all three corners.

lines.text: Put the compass point on $O$ and the pencil on $A$.
Draw the circle. It passes through $A$, $B$ and $C$. Leave all arcs showing.

workedSolution.finalAnswer: O\text{ is where the perpendicular bisectors meet; circle with centre }O\text{ through }A,B,C
